sentences.text: Malawisaurus was relatively small for a sauropod, with earlier estimates suggesting it reached lengths of about 15 meters and weighed about 10 tonnes, though a 2020 study revised these figures to approximately 11 meters and 2.8 tonnes.
It is one of the few titanosaurids for which skull material has been found.
Sidney H. Haughton originally described Malawisaurus dixeyi in 1928 as a species of Gigantosaurus, but Louis L. Jacobs and colleagues renamed the species Malawisaurus in 1993 based on new material.
The holotype specimen, which is the specific fossil the species is based on, is a partial skeleton identified as SAM 7405 from the Mwakasyunguti locality.
By definition, Malawisaurus is the most basal lithostrotian.
Malawisaurus is related to the Brazilian dinosaur Gondwanatitan, which was a member of the Aeolosaurini.
Malawisaurus fossils are found in the Dinosaur Beds of northern Malawi, dating to the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous, with a time range estimated between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
While the Dinosaur Beds are usually considered Barremian-Aptian, some researchers suggest they might be Late Cretaceous based on the vertebrate assemblage.
